summary: Pipeline saturation in us-west dedicated pool causing streaming timeouts and high tail latency
description: Issue summary: Customers using the us-west dedicated inference pool experienced a sudden degradation in throughput and a spike in streaming disconnects and 504/524 timeouts. Impact: Multiple NovaChat endpoints reported increases in tail latency (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.4s) and a 4-6% 5xx rate for generation requests between 2026-03-10 03:25 UTC and ongoing. Several streaming sessions dropped mid-response causing client-side errors and retries. Environment: prod dedicated pool in us-west (pool-id: dp-usw-61), serving-runtime v2.8.2, autoscaler v1.3. Investigation timeline and steps to reproduce: 1) At 03:20 UTC alerts fired on high GPU util and elevated request queues for dp-usw-61. 2) Support observed progressive queueing on the pool's work-queue: pending_batches metric rose from near-zero to 400+. 3) Attempts to reproduce by hitting NovaChat's pinned model showed delayed first-token times and streaming disconnects consistent with production symptoms. 4) Logs and metrics examined: GPU SM power draw and memory bandwidth saturation correlated with queue spikes; node-level telemetry showed elevated PCIe retries on three nodes. Observed behavior: - Sustained high GPU utilization on a subset of nodes with frequent power/clock throttling events. - Autoscaler did not scale up quickly enough; observed scale-up latency ~6 minutes vs target 90s. - Some nodes reported elevated PCIe errors which coincide with large throughput flows from an unexpected training-like job. Expected behavior: - Inference pool should serve low-latency requests with autoscaler responding within configured SLOs and strict isolation preventing heavy compute jobs from impacting inference nodes. Logs and relevant links: - Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/dp-usw-61?from=now-3h - Kibana traces: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/kibana#/discover/req-logs?query=dp-usw-61 - Slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02SUPPORT/p165) - Node logs: /var/log/pool/dp-usw-61/node-12-gpu0.log (attached snippets in ticket) Initial hypothesis: A customer workload (identified later as a mis-labeled batch job belonging to internal data-ops or a third-party partner) was scheduled on inference-capable nodes in the dedicated pool, saturating PCIe and memory bandwidth, causing noisy-neighbor effects. The autoscaler metric was configured to use CPU-based thresholds and did not account for GPU memory-bandwidth saturation, resulting in delayed scaling. Investigation notes: - Identified three nodes (node-10, node-11, node-12) with repeated GPU thermal throttling messages and high PCIe error counters. - SSH access to node-12 showed an unexpected long-running process (container id: c5a1b9) launching a distributed data-prep workload that appeared to use the GPU extensively. - Node labels show a mis-applied admission rule that allowed batch jobs to land on dp-usw pools after a recent scheduler config change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/commit/7f9a2a4). - Autoscaler config for dp-usw-61 used target_utilization: 0.65 on CPU, min_replicas: 1, max_replicas: 8; there is no separate GPU-bandwidth metric. - Queues backed up causing head-of-line blocking for streaming requests leading to disconnects. Immediate mitigation taken: - Isolated and cordoned node-10/11/12 for investigation to stop new tasks being scheduled. - Killed the mis-scheduled container c5a1b9 and restarted the node GPU drivers. - Manually scaled the pool to add 3 extra inference nodes from a warm spare pool; moved NovaChat traffic to the new nodes (partial failover). - Applied temporary admission rule to prevent non-inference jobs from being scheduled onto inference pools. Current status: In Progress. Remediation and next steps: - Short term: enforce strict nodeSelector and taints/tolerations in scheduler to block batch workloads from inference pools; update admission controller to reject jobs without "inference:true" label. - Medium term: update autoscaler to consider GPU-specific signals (memory bandwidth, PCIe retries, GPU SM utilization), and reduce scale-up cooldown to 90s for dedicated inference pools. - Long term: implement quota limits for per-customer persistent processes on dedicated pools and add automated detection of PCIe/memory-bandwidth saturation with alerting. - Post-incident: run root cause review and update runbooks; notify NovaChat CS with timeline and compensation options. Owner: SRE + Scheduler team. Follow-ups: linked INT-9942 (scheduler config rollback), infra PR to add GPU-bandwidth metric https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/6321, and a planned postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-15. Customer-facing note: Support has told NovaChat we are investigating and provided a temporary traffic-migration workaround. Resolution: ongoing; full RCA pending.

investigation: Telemetry indicates contention at the PCIe and GPU memory bandwidth layer rather than pure SM compute utilization. Head-of-line queueing on the pool's batcher caused significant delays for small low-latency streaming requests. Autoscaler not configured to react to this failure mode. Scheduler change allowed a noisy batch job into the pool. Root cause appears to be a combination of scheduler misconfiguration + autoscaler blind spot + a misbehaving scheduled job.
updates: 2026-03-10: Nodes cordoned and noisy container terminated; manual scale-out completed; customer traffic partially migrated.
2026-03-11: Scheduler admission rollback applied; temporary admission rule enforced to block non-inference containers.
